blocks.text: Transferring the risk of catastrophic system failure.
System Logic 01

Insurance is not an investment. It is a contract where you pay a small "Service Fee" (Premium) to a massive entity, so that when a "Critical Error" (Death, Accident, Fire) occurs, they bear the financial cost instead of you.
Brutal Truth: If you are buying insurance to "get money back," you are doing it wrong. That is a marketing trap.
🧾 Read the Contract

Insurance pays according to the policy wording and claim conditions. Check who is covered, what events are covered, exclusions, waiting periods, claim steps, and renewal terms before relying on a policy.
LEVEL 02: HARDWARE PROTECTION

Healthcare costs and medical inflation estimates vary by service, location, and source. A serious illness can create large costs; review policy limits and your ability to meet exclusions and out-of-pocket expenses.
🚫 No Room Rent Cap
If your policy has a cap (e.g., 1% of sum insured), and you take a better room, the company will cut your entire bill proportionally. It's a hidden kill-switch.
🚫 No Co-Pay
Co-pay means you pay a percentage of every bill. This is fine for small things, but catastrophic for a ₹20 Lakh bill.
🏥 Compare the Hospital Bill

For a health policy, examine room eligibility, co-payment, deductibles, sub-limits, pre-existing condition waiting periods, network hospitals, and restoration benefits. A large sum insured does not remove restrictions elsewhere in the contract.
LEVEL 03: LIFE PROTOCOL

Traditional savings-linked insurance policies combine insurance and savings features, with benefits defined by the contract. Compare guaranteed and non-guaranteed benefits, charges, cover, surrender terms, and tax treatment; avoid assuming one return or inflation rate applies to every policy.
The FIN-OS Formula

A life-cover estimate should consider dependants’ needs, liabilities, existing assets and insurance, future goals, and the years of support required. Use the linked calculator as an estimate, not a universal formula.
A sample calculation is only a starting point. The appropriate cover depends on household circumstances and should be reviewed as income, debt, dependants, and assets change.
👪 Estimate the Need

Think through the income your dependants would need, outstanding debts, existing assets, other cover, and how long support may be required. Treat any income multiple as a starting estimate, not a universal answer.

✅ Claim-Ready Checklist

Keep policy details and insurer contact information accessible, understand how to notify a claim, and retain bills and records. Recheck cover when dependants, debt, income, or employer benefits change. Confirm current tax treatment with an authoritative source.
